facts.text: Downtown Indianapolis grew from the original 1821 Mile Square plat, expanding beyond the one‑square‑mile grid to include several historic neighborhoods.
The city’s first union train station opened in 1853, making Indianapolis Union Station the world’s first true union station.
The 1904 Indianapolis Traction Terminal on Market Street once handled 500 trains daily, becoming the largest interurban station in the world.
Indiana Avenue in downtown’s northwest quadrant houses the Crispus Attucks Museum and the Kurt Vonnegut Museum and Library, celebrating African‑American heritage and literary history.
The Central Library’s five‑block Indiana World War Memorial Plaza sits just east of Meridian Street, honoring veterans with a prominent memorial.
Downtown is bordered by I‑65, I‑70, and the White River, placing it near Marion County’s geographic center and the confluence of Fall Creek and the White River.
